about: Patterns only, reviewed by hand: lines GuestTest2's log sweep drops, as re.search over a normalized line (guest_judge.normalize: numbers are N, hex HEX, times TIME). all and host: every guest (host: below); the others by the spec's checks.pm. A pattern marked list: also drops the indented lines under the line it matches (package names, wrapped). A new pattern re-runs only those guests. Keep it package-manager chatter: a real error must never match. The accepted per-guest lines are never here: they live on the Mac (guest-baselines), since they can hold machine IDs and hostnames.

hbsd, ld-elf.so.1's Tainted line: at every boot, /etc/rc.d/ldconfig (FreeBSD 15's) asks the run-time linker for its default path with /libexec/ld-elf.so.1 -v, and HardenedBSD's rtld refuses to be run directly while hardening.harden_rtld is 1, its default (sysctl hardening.harden_rtld=0 makes the same command print 'Default lib path /lib:/usr/lib'; seen on hardenedbsd15 and hardenedbsd15-zfs, GuestTest2 t2v-20261118T0027-d7c8, before and after the update).  Harmless: the hints file then lacks /lib and /usr/lib, which rtld searches anyway as its built-in default

host, every guest's whatever its package manager: lines that say what host the guest was placed on (its CPU, the firmware QEMU gives it, its clocks), never what the guest or its update did.  One guest landing on a host it hadn't run on made them new, though the same line was accepted on other guests: in GuestTest2 passes 4-6 of 2026-11-18 (t2v-20261118T0617-4a11, -0942-226e, -1159-2749) the Ryzen 5600H hosts' (chopin, cinqcent) unstable-TSC and CPU-feature lines, amd_pstate's CPPC lines on every AMD host, choubox's Intel CPU in a BSD's boot banner, chronyd stepping a clock the host set.  And what a BSD loader's spinner leaves of its console output (normalize erases what a backspace does, but the loader's dual console writes each character twice, the spinner unevenly between them, as fast as the host loads): a line of spinner characters alone, and its doubled lines ('//bboooott//kkeerrnneell//zzffss..kkoo ssiizzee ...'), unless a doubled error word is in one.  Kept out on purpose: a kernel WARNING, BUG or oops and its trace, even one the host's CPU triggers (choubox's Intel ITS thunks give 'CPA detected W^X violation' with a WARNING in set_memory.c: it is classed per guest, or fixed), failed units, I/O and file system errors.  Each pattern is the whole line's form, anchored, so a real error in the same words never matches (test_guest_judge.HostLines)

tukit (aeon, microos): transactional-update runs zypper inside its snapshot, so zypper's patterns, and its scriptlets' and preloads' progress lines (GuestTest2 t2v-20261118T1159-2749: spec.json named #tukit before there was one, so these guests had only all's and host's)

guix (guix15, guix15-bios): guix pull's and guix system reconfigure's chatter (substitute lookups, progress bars, download rates, /gnu/store paths, grafts, profile hooks, activation, Shepherd's service starts) from both guests' 2026-11-14 update.logs on Chopin.  And the serial console's early boot (GuestTest2 t2v-20261118T2038-21eb): the initrd's Guile (PID 1) has no /proc yet, so Boehm GC warns 'GC Warning: pthread_getattr_np or pthread_attr_getstack failed for main thread' and 'GC Warning: Could not open /proc/stat' and finds its stack by probing, a SIGSEGV it handles, which the kernel logs for PID 1 anyway ('init[1]: segfault at ... in guile[...]', its 'Code:' line with the probe's movzbl (%rax),%edi at <0f> b6 38, call e8), on the console and again from syslogd.  The 16550's 16-byte FIFO cuts the warnings into 16-byte pieces ('GC Warning: pthr', 'ead_getattr_np o', 'r pthread_attr_g', 'etstack failed f', 'or main thread'; 'GC Warning: Coul', 'd not open /proc', '/stat') and the kernel's lagging console output lands between them, so each boot glues other lines on ('GC Warning: pthr PM: Magic number: N:N:N', 'etstack failed f Code: ...'); syslogd's echo and the getty prompt get the next kernel line glued on too.  A glued-on kernel line is dropped only when it is the probe's segfault or has no error word (err, fail, warn, BUG, oops, panic, call trace, segfault, timed out, ...): any other segfault, and a Code: line without the probe's bytes, stay judged.  Download rates: store names have dots (libgit2-1.9.1-debug).  Kept out on purpose: Guile backtraces (In ..., N:N N (...)), 'guix system: warning:' and error lines.  truenas (truenas25, truenas25-mirror): empty until the first probe boot's journal shows the middleware's chatter

Retried downloads and per-boot chance matches whose values change every run, so a line accepted for one guest was new on its next run (GuestTest2 t2v-20261119T1434-e089).  pacman (the Arch family): curl's 'Operation too slow' on one file ('error: failed retrieving file 'breeze-6.8.3-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst' from geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com : Operation too slow. Less than 1 bytes/sec transferred the last 10 seconds', a .sig too; endeavouros-grub), which in-guest.sh's Linux.pacman fetched() greps for ('failed retrieving file') and retries up to 10 times ('a download failed: pacman again in 30 s (N of 10)'); a failure that persists still fails the update there.  Only the too-slow form: another curl error, and pacman's other error lines, stay judged.  zypper and tukit (tumbleweed, leap16; aeon, microos): a preload that one mirror answers with an HTTP error ('Preloading: diffutils-3.12-2.1.x86_64.rpm [Error: "The requested URL returned error: 404", trying next mirror.]'), which zypper itself takes from the next mirror, failing the transaction if none has it; and the repository refresh's progress line, which the gpg-key lines cut off after one to three dots ('Retrieving repository 'repo-oss (16.1)' metadata [..').  Kept out: 'end of response with N bytes missing' and any other preload error, and a refresh line with anything after its dots.  guix (guix15, guix15-bios): linux-libre's CONFIG_PM_TRACE_RTC reads the RTC at boot as a suspend trace ('PM:   Magic number: N:N:N', accepted per guest) and names whatever device or source line its hash matches by chance, a different one each boot: '<bus or driver> <device>: hash matches' (pci 0000:00:1f.3, pci 0000:00:03.0) and 'PM:   hash matches <file>:<line>' (drivers/base/power/main.c:1424), on the console or from syslogd; only the fixed 'hash matches' message, anchored

apt (every apt guest): in-guest.sh's Linux.apt runs apt-get update up to 60 times 15 s apart and prints a failed try as one line, 'in-guest: apt-get update failed (try N of 60): ' and that try's first E: line, or its first Err: line and the reason under it ('E: Failed to fetch https://archive.neon.kde.org/user/dists/noble/InRelease  502  Bad Gateway [IP: 1.2.3.4 443]'; neon24, a FREEZE run 2026-11-20, which passed on try 4).  The try that worked is printed alone, so the failed tries' own lines never reach the log; a failure that persists prints its last try whole and fails the update there, so its lines stay judged.  Only that summary line, anchored

in-guest.sh's other retry loops (2026-11-20), as apt-get update's above: each try's output goes to a file first (/run on Linux and Guix, /tmp on DragonFly, illumos and Redox), a try tried again is one line, the retry line it always printed with the first of the try's lines that made it a retry appended ('in-guest: a download failed: pacman again in 30 s (1 of 10): error: failed retrieving file ...'), and the try that worked, or the last that failed, is printed whole.  So a failed try's own lines never reach the log, and its one line is accepted for that loop's guests: apt (fetched()'s download and lock retries, elementary's flatpak update, the snap refresh after apt), pacman, rpm-ostree, xbps, guix (guix pull, guix system reconfigure), dragonfly (pkg, git ls-remote, the base system's shallow clone), portage (emerge --sync), snap (Ubuntu Core's refresh --list and --no-wait) and ips (pkg refresh --full, and pkg update that couldn't reach a publisher's repository: '(try N of 10)').  Redox's loop is the same but runs on no guest yet (the redox guest is a console probe), so redox has no pattern.  A failure that persists prints its last try whole and fails the update, so its lines stay judged.  Only each retry line's own words, anchored
